title: About Us | Finance Department Government of Meghalaya
content: Finance Department The Role and function of Finance Department are laid down in the Rules of Executive Business. The department is primarily responsible for the financial administration and management of the State Finances. Some the main functions of the department are preparation of budget and statement of estimated revenues and expenditure to be laid down before the State Legislature; Examination of the proposals for increase or reduction of taxes; state borrowings and provision of Government Guarantees against loans raised by PSUs and otherentities; laying down of appropriate financial rules for guidance of other department that are responsible for maintenance of proper accounts and action to enforce accountability on such matters; preparation of estimates of receipts and disbursements and keeping watch on State Government fiscal balances, ways and means operations etc.; framing of various rules regulating the pay, leave of person in service of the state Government and rules regulating the number, grading or cadre emolument of posts; laying down of appropriate financial rules for guidance of all departments and other entities etc.

title: Finance Audit & Funds Branch | Finance Department Government of Meghalaya
headings: Audit Committees constituted in the Department | Matter related to various Funds dealt by the Department | Other Matters dealt by the Department: | Key Contacts
content: Finance Audit & Funds Branch Finance (AF) as the same suggests deals in matters relating to Audit and Funds. Audit matters include Inspection Report, Draft Paragraphs, C&A.G. Reports, Arrear in accounts of PSUs. The Department acts as a monitoring authority in these matters and all correspondences regarding these matters are recorded in the Department. The Department also issues relevant instruction to the Departments in connection with these matters. Audit Committees constituted in the Department Audit Committee Meetings: The Department deputes a representative to the Audit Committee Meetings for settlement of Inspection Reports. DAAC (Departmental Audit & Accounts Committee): The Department issues instructions to all Departments to convene meetings and to settle matters relating to Audit. SAAC (State Audit & Accounts Committee): Under the Chairmanship of the Chief Secretary, a State Level Committee meeting is convened every year with the Principal Accountant General (Audit) for settlement of Draft Paras relating to Audit of various Departments. Matter related to various Funds dealt by the Department G.P.F.: The Department conveys approval in respect of GPF applications in accordance with the Meghalaya GPF Rules 2020 C.E.A. (Children Education Advance): The Department provides funds for allotment of Children Education Advance to Govt. Employees every year. H.B.A. to A.I.S. Officers: The Department provides fund for allotment of House Building Advances to AIS Officers every year. Ex-gratia payment: Fund is provided for payment to employees who died in harness. Other Matters dealt by the Department: T.A.: Dealing with T.A. claim as per TA Rules. Mileage Allowance is also included in the TA/DA for different types of vehicles used for official tours. House Rent Allowance: The Department conveys approval to claim on House Rent Allowance as per rate fixed by Finance (P.R.) Department vide No. F(PR)48/2009/1, dated 17th September, 2009. Write Off: All matters relating to write off has to be approved by this Department. Arrear Pay: All claims for arrear pay has to be approved by this Department. Facilities of Ministers, Parliamentary Secretaries, Chairman, Co-Chairman, Vice-Chairman and Deputy Chairman: These orders/circulars are revised by this Department from time to time. L.T.C. (Leave Travel Concession). Refund of Revenue. Air Journeys: This Department also conveys approval for air journeys performed on Training, Study Tour, Medical Treatment, etc. List of Officers and Employees ( As in 25th August 2020) PDF 39.3 KB View Key Contacts Joint Secretary - S - 2687/9436108063 Under Secretary - S - 2709

content: Finance Economic Affairs Branch The Department is primarily meant for effecting proper financial administration in the State. The main functions of the Department are indicated below: Preparation of skeleton Budget in respect of Revenue Expenditure of the State. Preparation of forecast of resources. Watching the flow of revenue such as release of Art. 275 grants, share of Central Taxes, on-account payment of Central Assistance for State Plan Schemes, Ways and Means Advance for Centrally Sponsored Schemes, Central Sector Schemes, NLCPR, EAP and N.E.C. Plan Schemes. Watching the flow of receipts and out goings, finding out resources for the State and monitoring the reports on collection of taxes and loans. Watching the progress of small savings collection, claim of reimbursement from the Government of India by the Department concerned. Introduction and enforcement of Economy Measures, Financial Control and Discipline. Watching the share between the State Government and the District Councils on Motor Vehicles Tax/ Royalties on Minor/Major/Professional Tax etc. Watching the release of certain grants by Government of India and follow up action for preferring claims by the Department, such as Border Roads, Jails, Civil Defense and Home Guards, etc. Policy etc on Natural Calamities following on the recommendation of the Finance Commission and watching the release of Central share by the Government of India. Fixation of the rate of interest on various loans sanctioned by the State Government. Matter relating to Additional Resources Mobilization. Dearness Allowances etc. Financial matters. Dealing with outside file that come from Finance (EC) Department for the purpose of release of funds/additional requirements. Digital Payments & Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) Cell. Civil Deposits & Treasury Current Account ADB Project on Supporting Human Capital Development in Meghalaya. FRBM Act. Monthly Civil Accounts. VDMS, IFMS, CPSMS Monthly Statement and Daily Reports on Receipt & Expenditure from DAT/TOs. State Government Guarantee Ways and Means: Watching and monitoring the daily cash balance position of the State Government. Monitoring the daily Advices from the ministry and Clearances memos from Reserve Bank of India on daily basis. Monitoring the report on investment of Cash Balance and Government of India Treasury Bills. Preparation of Monthly forecast on receipts and expenditure of the State Government. Arranging temporary Ways and Means. Advance either from the R.B.I. or from the Government of India in the event/likelihood of shortfall of cash position of the State and regulation of overdraft. Maintenance of ledgers for all loans raised from the market Government of India, L.I.G., G.I.C, N.C.D.C., N.A.B.A.R.D. etc. and arranging for timely repayment of principal and interest with a view to avoid penal interest. Make arrangement for floatation of market loan etc Investment in Government of India securities matters connected to. Scarcity of Coins and Demonetization of Currency Action whereon. Shortage of cash in the Banks, arrangement of remittances. Monthly closing balance statement from R.B.I. and the A.G. matters relating to. State Finance Secretary's Meeting convened by RBI/GOI. Matters related to Finance Commission Analysis of the trends in the receipts and expenditure of the respective Departments. Follow up action on the recommendation of Finance Commission Collect and update information on various items relating to state economy including financial working of the state enterprises. Collection and compilation of data/information and preparation of forecast of receipts and expenditure and memorandum for submission to the Finance Commission. State Finance Commission. Institutional Finance Act as Nodal Department between the Nationalized Banks and the State Government Department in respect of any matters between the State Government and the Banking Institution. Follow-up action for the expansion of banking network in the State for the purpose of increasing credit/deposit ratio opening of bank branches at different centres of the state. Liaison with all the Banking and Financial Institutions operating in the State Monitor and watch the progress of development in the implementation of State Government's link with Bank Finance. Matters involving all District Consultative Committee, State Level Bankers Committee and all other banking/financial institutional fora. Closely monitor and watch the implementation of the District Credit Plans and other bankable Scheme over and above linkages of Government sponsored schemes with bank finance for the improvement of the economic conditions of the poor people. Women Economic Empowerment through Financial Inclusion, Financial Inclusion Committee, Designing A2F Programme. PMEGP, PMMY, PMJDY, PMSBY, PMJJDY, APY, Stand Up India. Technical Committee for fixing the Scale of Finance. Monitoring and Loan Recovery Cell To take action to ensure flow of institutional credit in the State and closely monitoring the same investment in the flow of credit to the State. To interact with the Banking institution and other financial institution and to sort out problems investment in the flow of credit to the State. To monitor and watch the function and operation of Non Bank Financial Company (NBFC) in the State. Monitoring the expenditure on Non-Plan schemes. Monitoring the collection of Taxes, duties under different taxation and recoveries of loan and advances and measures for improvement. Monitoring the progress of sanction for implementation of expenditure under Non Plan /Plan. Monitoring monthly, quarterly return on: Collection of arrears and current demand of taxes and non tax revenue. Collection of arrears and current demand of loans and advances. Data collection, compilation for incorporation in the report of the comptrollerand Auditor General of India. Matters connected with short term loans for agricultural inputs and recovery loans sanctioned by the State Government to Government Department/Public Undertaking etc. Public Enterprises Branch: Monitor the functions and performance of all public enterprise establishments in the State with particular reference to the internal resources of the Public Enterprises and their contribution towards the State Plan. All matters relating to meeting etc. of the State Public Sector Undertakings, Government Agencies Companies where Finance Secretary is a Director/Member of the Board of Management. VRS to employees of SPSUs. Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) Cell To study the Schemes, classify them and re-examine existing process flows and fund flow of the same To develop Web based IT applications and facilitate automation of process flow and funds flow. To monitor and supervise the implementation of DBT on regular basis. Any other related matters. content: Finance Establishment Branch Finance (E) Department functions as a referral Department for interpretation of FRs and SRs, Financial Rules and all State Services and Delegation of Financial Power Rules concerning all the employees under the State Government. The Department administers the following Rules: Meghalaya Financial Rules Meghalaya Fundamental Rules and Subsidiary Rules Meghalaya Treasury Rules Delegations of Financial Power Rules It is responsible for interpretation and advice to other Departments in respect of any issues / cases under the ambit of all the four above mentioned Rules. It also functions as a referral Department in respect of - Scrutiny of the Service Rules Re-employment on contract basis Permanent Absorption Declaring of officers as DDO It also deals with all matters related with - Meghalaya Finance Service Meghalaya Accounts Service Meghalaya Audit Service. Cyber Treasury Govt. Employees Database National e-Governance Plan Issues with Agency Banks Matters relating to PFMS. It functions as the Nodal Division in respect of - Matters related in general with other Divisions of Finance Department Matters related with general RTI cases that relates to Finance. Dealing with matters not allocated to any Division of Finance Department. headings: Powers and Duties of its Officers and Employees: | Procedure followed in the Decision Making Process, including channels of supervision and accountability: | Finance Pay Revision Organisational Chart
content: Finance Pay Revision Branch Finance (Pay Revision) has been created with the sole objective to implement the recommendations of the Meghalaya Pay Commissions, constituted from time to time by Government on matters relating to the structure of emoluments and service conditions of different categories of State Government employees, keeping in regard the inter-services relationship, the total packet of benefits available to them and the resources of the State; existing structure of pension including Death-Cum-Retirement Gratuity and other retirement benefits and a variety of compensatory allowances available to the employees and the pay package and retirement benefits to the State Government employees. The Department functions at the Secretariat level only, having no subordinate offices under its control. Its duties are service-related matters concerning the pay, allowances, etc. of the employees of the State Government. The Department is entrusted with the following work: Implementation of the recommendations of the Meghalaya Pay Commissions, as accepted by Government. Checking and approval of the Initial Pay Statements of all non-gazetted and gazetted employees drawing pay from the establishment pay bills. Examination of cases referred by Government departments for views/comments and concurrence in the matter of scales of pay and allowances of the employees. Concurrence to regularization of the services of Work-Charged persons serving under various Departments of the Government. Other residual matters that may be referred to the Department from time to time where the pay and allowances, pay anomalies, etc. of the employees of the State Government are concerned. Stepping up of Pay arise due to fixation of pay as per Initial Pay Statement (IPS), Assured Career Progression Scheme (ACPS) and Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme (MACPS). Concurrence on Monetary Compensation for Holidays Forgone. Powers and Duties of its Officers and Employees: The Department is under the control of Additional Chief Secretary, Finance / Principal Secretary, Finance and assisted by Secretary, Joint Secretary and Deputy Secretary.The duties, functions of the officers and its employees are as laid down in the Meghalaya Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure, 1993. Procedure followed in the Decision Making Process, including channels of supervision and accountability: All matters received in the branch are processed by the Assistants, Superintendent, etc., as per duties and functions laid down in the Meghalaya Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure, 1983 and put up to the Officers for decision as per Work Flow Chart below:- Finance Pay Revision Organisational Chart (opens the full-size chart in a new tab) Finance Pay Revision Organisational Chart View full size (opens in a new tab) Download (JPG) Directory of Officers and Employees: as on 17/09/2020 PDF 51 KB View

The Cell also functions as referral department in respect of: Re-employment on contract basis Permanent Absorption Revision of Pension for AIS officers Matter related with general R.T.I cases that relates to pension cases. title: Directorate of Accounts and Treasuries | Finance Department Government of Meghalaya
headings: Directorate | District Treasuries | Sub-Treasuries | Account units | Functions and Duties | The duties of its officers and employees | Meghalaya Subordinate Treasury Accounts Service:- | Meghalaya Subordinate Accounts Service:- | Categories of documents that are held by it or under its control:
content: Directorate of Account and Treasuries Directorate The Directorate of Accounts and Treasuries was established in the year 1972 and is under the administrative control of Finance (Establishment) Department, Government of Meghalaya. The Directorate is headed by the Director of Accounts and Treasuries who in turn is assisted by a Joint Director, Deputy Director and an Instructor of Central Training Institute, all from the Meghalaya Finance Service. The administrative hierarchy is further assisted in the performance of their duties by Accounts staff, technical staff for system management and a number of ministerial and Grade - IV staff. District Treasuries At the District level, there is one District Treasury in every District of the State with the exception of East Khasi Hills where there are two Treasuries. Each Treasury is headed by a Treasury Officer, a member from the Meghalaya Finance Service, assisted by (1) Assistant Treasury Officer/ Accountant, Senior Accounts Assistants and Junior Accounts Assistants, from the Meghalaya Subordinate Treasury Accounts Service. (2) Senior Assistant System Administrator (Technical) for system management and (3) Grade - IV staff. Sub-Treasuries Currently, there is one Sub-Treasury each in four Civil Sub-Divisions in the State. Each sub-treasury is headed by a Treasury Officer, a member from the Meghalaya Finance Service, assisted by (1) Accountant, Senior Accounts Assistants and Junior Accounts Assistants, from the Meghalaya Subordinate Treasury Accounts Service, (2) Assistant System Administrator (Technical) for system management and (3) Grade - IV staff. Account units Accounts unit were set up in every Cheque Drawing offices of PWD, PHE, Water Resources, Urban Affairs etc departments.. Each Account Unit is headed by the Accounts Officer and assisted by Senior Divisional Accountants and Junior Divisional Accountants, all from the Meghalaya Accounts Service. Accounts Officers cadre are under the Administrative control of Finance (Establishment) Department where as Senior Divisional Accountant (SDA) and Junior Divisional Accountant (JDA) are under the control of Directorate of Accounts & Treasuries. At present there are 9 Heads of Department (5 Cheque Drawing Authority and 4 Bill Drawing DDO), 2 Meghalaya Houses at Delhi and Mumbai, 18 Circles and 70 Divisions where Accounts Officers and Accounts staffs are posted. The sanctioned strength of these officers is as below: Accounts Officer = 76 Nos. Senior Divisional Accountant = 54 Nos. Junior Division Accountant = 173 Nos. Functions and Duties The Directorate has both Administrative and Statutory functions as under Administrative control of all Treasuries and Sub-Treasuries Overseeing the functions of Treasuries as primary units of fiscal system of the State, regulating and facilitating the receipt of Govt. moneys and the withdrawal of govt. fund in accordance with the rules and regulations framed by the Finance Department and submission of monthly accounts to the office of the Accountant General (A&E) Meghalaya Overseeing the functions of all accounts units in cheque drawing Offices, viz., PWD, PHE, Water Resources, Urban Affairs, etc Administrative control of Meghalaya Subordinate Treasury Accounts Service; Administrative Control of Meghalaya Accounts Service; Training of Finance Officers, Accounts and Audit Officers, other Accounts & Audit staff, UDA & LDA of Heads of departments/ District offices/ District Councils. Etc., in all finance/accounts and audit matters. Nodal Officer in respect of New Pension Scheme. Cyber Treasury. Employee and Pension Database. The duties of its officers and employees Officers of the Directorate of Accounts & Treasuries and their duties Officers Duty Director The Director of Accounts & Treasuries (DAT) is responsible to supervise, control and affectively run the Directorate. All the decision making are taken at the level of the Head of Department except those that are not provided for, in different rules/instructions. The DAT is also the Administrative Head who controls the cadres of Meghalaya Accounts Service and the Meghalaya Subordinate Treasury Accounts Service. DAT is also vested with the responsibility of conducting training to the Officers of Meghalaya Finance Service, Accounts and Audit staff, Ministerial staff of the Heads of Department/District Officer etc. Various programmes are also organized for imparting training to the Officers and staff on the new initiatives and projects undertaken by the Directorate. Joint Director of Accounts & Treasuries To assist the Director of Accounts & Treasuries on all matters aforementioned. Deputy Director of Accounts & Treasuries To assist the Director of Accounts & Treasuries and Joint Director of Accounts & Treasuries on all matters stated above. Instructor To conduct training to Officers of M.F.S., staff of the Accounts Service and Treasury staff in different capacities. Treasury Officer The Treasury Officer is primarily responsible for financial transactions pertaining to receipts and payments on account of the State Government relating to various Government Departments. He is also responsible for timely and prompt submission of the monthly compiled Accounts relating to such transactions to the Accountant General. For proper discharge of the above functions, the Treasury Officer is to strictly observe all rules prescribed by the Government for his guidance with regard to the daily routine of Treasury work. Besides the above, the office establishment under the Director of Accounts & Treasuries consists of the following:- Technical staff and their duties Technical staff Duties System Administrator System Management on TreasuryNET Application, Employee and Pension Database, Pension Automated System, New Pension Scheme, DivisionNET, etc. Programme Assistant Grade - I Technical matter under Treasury NET/Pension Automated System & New Pension Scheme. Programme Assistant Grade - II Maintenance of Stock Inventory of all computer hardware and peripherals. Data Entry Operator Employee Database matters. Computer Clerk Daily Report of Expenditure and Receipts from Treasury NET. Compilation & Uploading of NPS Contribution for the whole State. Ministerial staff and their duties Ministerial staff Duties Superintendent Supervision of Establishment matters. Steno Grade - II Steno work. Upper Divisional Assistant Establishment & Clerical works. Lower Divisional Accountant Establishment & Clerical works. Typist Typing work. Duftry Bank Duty. Driver Driving allotted car. Grade - IV Dak duties and miscellaneous works. Meghalaya Subordinate Treasury Accounts Service:- Staffs Duties Assistant Treasury Officer To assist the Treasury Officer Senior Assistant System Administrator (District Treasuries) System Management in respective Treasuries. Assistant System Administrator (Sub-Treasuries) System Management in respective Treasuries. Accountant Receipts, Payment and Accounting of Government transactions Senior Account Assistant Receipts, Payment and Accounting of Government transactions Junior Account Assistant Receipts, Payment and Accounting of Government transactions Meghalaya Subordinate Accounts Service:- Staffs Duties Accounts Officer To assist the Divisional Officer in all financial matters, establishment, etc. Senior Divisional Accountant To assist the Accounts Officer. Junior Divisional Accountant To assist the Senior Divisional Accountant and Accounts Officer. The decision is taken strictly in accordance with policies framed by Government of Meghalaya and Rules & Regulations on the subject. The dealing assistant deals with the case and submits to the Superintendent who in turn sends the case to his superior, i.e. the Deputy Director. The Deputy Director will minutely examine the case and send it to Joint Director who examines it and forwards it to the Director for final approval. The Department discharges its various functions and duties by following the below mentioned Rules and Manuals:- Meghalaya Treasury Rules, 1985. Meghalaya Financial Rules, 1981. Meghalaya Fundamental Rules and Subsidiary Rules, 1984. Meghalaya Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1983. Meghalaya Civil Services (GPF) Rules, 1985. Meghalaya Travelling Allowances Rules, 1985. Accounts Code - Volume - II. Budget Manual. Contingency manual. Govt. Accounting Rules 1990 Meghalaya Delegation of Financial Powers Rules 2006 Manual & records: Records of Payment (T.V. Nos) Records of Receipt (Challan Nos.) Categories of documents that are held by it or under its control: PPOs of Pensioners. Cheque Books issued to Divisions. Transit Register issued to DDOs. Challans issued to Vendors. Stamps (Judicial & Non-Judicial) issued to vendors. Personal Files of employees. Service Books of employees. Annual Confidential Report. Cash Books. Stamp paper Registers. Plus and Minus Memorandum. content: Directorate of Local Fund Audit The Director of Local Fund Audit was bifurcated from the Directorate of Accounts and Treasuries and Examiner of Local Accounts on the 1stFebruary, 1990. It was earlier known to the State Government as well as to the public as the Office of the Examiner of Local Accounts and in the 2015, its nomenclature was changed to the Directorate of Local Fund Audit. The office is currently located in the Nokrek Building (3rd Secretariat) at Lower Lachumiere, Shillong, East Khasi Hills District, Meghalaya. At present, the Audit works are being carried out by the Outside Audit Party (OAP) throughout the State in various Auditee Institutions on the authority issued by the Directorate. The Directorate has established the first District Office at Tura, West Garo Hills District in the year,2013 and is headed by an Officer not below the rank of Deputy Director. The Directorate of Local Fund Audit is headed by a Director and has one Joint Director, one Deputy Director, three Assistant Directors i.e; two in the Headquarter at Shillong and one at Tura in the District Office, Audit Officers, Auditors and Assistant Auditors for running the daily activities and general administration of the day-to-day works of the Directorate. Sanctioned strength of the Directorate:- Assistant Director of Local Fund Audit - 3 Nos. Audit Officer - 27 Nos. Auditor - 35 Nos. Assistant Auditor - 72 Nos. Superintendent - 1 No. U.D. Assistant - 4 Nos. L.D. Assistant - 5 Nos. Typist - 8 Nos. Roles and Responsibilities Officers and their duties Officers Roles and Responsibilities Director The Director Local Fund Audit (DLFA) is responsible to supervise, control and effectively run the Directorate. All the decisions are taken at the level of the Head of Department, except those that are not provided for in different Rules and instructions. The Director Local Fund Audit is also the Administrative Head who controls the overall functioning of the Office. The Director of Local Fund Audit is also vested with powers to examine and carry out the audit of accounts of Local Bodies and accounts of various Departments of the Govt., Aided Education institutions, others organisation as specified in the Local Audit Manual and such other accounts of organisations/offices etc. as may be entrusted by the Govt. from time to time in this regard and to pass and issue Audit/Inspection Reports thereon and settlement of observation, if any. Joint Director, Deputy Director & Assistant Director (Shillong) To assist the Director of Local Fund Audit. Assistant Director of Local Fund Audit (Tura). He is the Head of the Office in his respective jurisdiction and exercise all powers as Head of the District Office. His duties also include the general supervision and co-ordination of the audit field staff posted in his jurisdiction. For this purpose, inspections during the course of audit will be made by him and he will render necessary guidance to the audit field staff. He examine, approve, issue and settle the audit inspection reports in respect of L.P., U.P. School within his jurisdiction, or others additional works as may assigned by the Director of Local Fund Audit from time to time. Audit Officer To conduct the Audit of all the Schools, Colleges and any other Auditee Institution. Auditor & Assistant Auditor To Assist the Audit Officer The procedure followed in the decision making process The decision is taken strictly in accordance with policies framed by Government of Meghalaya and Rules and Regulations on the subject. The concerned staff dealing with the case puts up and submitsthe report/case to the Superintendent who inturn refer the case to his/her Superior, i.e. the Deputy Director. The Deputy Director will minutely examine the case and send it to the Joint Director who examines and recommend the same to the Director for final approval. title: Directorate of Small Savings | Finance Department Government of Meghalaya
headings: Organization | Functions and Duties | Types of Small Savings | Key Contacts
content: Directorate of Small Savings The particulars of its organization, functions and duties: Organization The Directorate of Small Savings functions under the administrative control of Finance (Budget) Department, Government of Meghalaya. The Directorate is headed by the Director of Small Savings who in turn is assisted by Upper Division Assistants and Lower Division Assistants. Small Savings constitute a major resource to execute welfare activities of the Government. A major portion of the net collections under Small Savings is returned to the State by the Government of India as long term-soft loan. The long repayment schedule makes it an excellent resource of the State for investment in improvement /development of infrastructure like Roads, Drinking water, Sewerage, Hospitals, Schools etc. In order to increase the resources, the State Government is taking all efforts to mobilize Savings. However, on the recommendations of the Fourteenth Finance Commission, the State has discontinued availing loans from the National Small Savings Fund w.e.f. 1st April, 2016. Small Savings offer the best and safest avenue of investment of household savings. Small Savings scripts are guaranteed by Government and thus completely secure. Functions and Duties The Directorate of Small Savings is mainly concerned with the promotion of various Small Savings Schemes formulated by Government of India. Small Savings Schemes are implemented through the Department of Posts, and 15 year Public Provident Fund Scheme is implemented through Head Post offices as well as Banks. title: Privacy Policy | Finance Department Government of Meghalaya
content: Thank you for visiting the website of Finance Department, Government of Meghalaya, and reviewing our privacy policy. We collect no personal information, like names or addresses, when you visit our website. If you chose to provide that information to us, it is only used to fulfil your request for information. If you choose to provide us with personal information - like an e-mail address or postal address, we use that information to respond to your message, and to help you get the information you've requested. We only share the information you give us with another Government agency if your question relates to that agency, or as otherwise required by law. Our website never collects information or creates individual profiles for commercial marketing. While you must provide an e-mail address for a localised response to any incoming questions or comments to us, we recommend that you do NOT include any personal information.

title: Centralized Pension Payment System and Pensioner Self-Verification System | Finance Department Government of Meghalaya
content: Centralized Pension Payment System and Pensioner Self-Verification System The payment of monthly Pension to the Pensioners have been automated for all Treasuries and Sub-Treasuries in the state. The Pensioners need not come to the Treasury to submit their pension bills every month but the payment is processed centrally and the amount is credited directly to bank account of the pensioner. The State Government has adopted biometric system as an alternative automated method of verifying the identity of a living pensioner. Pensioner can do self verification through Kiosk Machine which has been installed in various treasuries and sub-treasuries and a number of banks. Plans have been drawn up to install the KIOSK in more Banks and other important public offices like Offices of the Deputy Commissioner etc.

title: DivisionNet (Online Computerization of Divisions) | Finance Department Government of Meghalaya
content: DivisionNet (Online Computerization of Divisions) NIC Meghalaya has taken up the computerization of the Accounting Sections of the Divisions of different Works Department such as PWD, PHE, Forest etc. The online application has been developed and it is being implemented in many Divisional Offices under PWD, Water Resources etc. Salient features includes (i) Uses the Work flow concept, building of Contractors/Supplier database, online validation of Bills, preparation and printing of cheques, generation of Bill Extract Form and DDO Advice etc.

title: Integrated Financial Management System | Finance Department Government of Meghalaya
content: Integrated Financial Management System (IFMS) (opens the full-size chart in a new tab) Integrated Financial Management System View full size (opens in a new tab) Download (JPG Size: 38 KB) The Meghalaya Integrated Financial Management System URL: is an ICT based fiscal and financial management information system that provides financial information to the State government in general and Finance department in particular to monitor the receipt and expenditure incurred by various departments and to manage and report their financial activities. With the implementation of the Online Treasury Computerisation (TreasuryNET), the financial transactions (receipt & expenditure) from various treasuries and sub-treasuries in the state can be integrated and published in this portal. The IFMS is designed to address and to act as a Financial Information, Administration and Management of the State Government. The portal depicts the up-to date Compiled Payment & Receipt Data from all district treasuries and sub-treasuries in the state. Finance Department and HODs can get the DDO-wise expenditure details of various grants up to voucher level. Finance Department and Tax Revenue Department can reconcile the receipt figure with the figure from the treasuries. Users can get the detail information of daily revenue receipt of various revenue earning departments like Taxation, Excise, Minerals etc. Details of the expenditure incurred by the Remittance Department like PWD, PHED, Soil Conservation, Forest etc. is available at a glance. Exception Reports are provided for decision makers.

title: New Defined Contribution Pension Scheme | Finance Department Government of Meghalaya
content: New Defined Contribution Pension Scheme New Defined Contribution Pension Scheme was started during the year 2010-11 vide Government Office Memorandum No. FEM(PC)7/2007/Pt-II/66 dt. 24.03.2010 with effective date from 01.04.2010. The scheme is applicable to all regular Government employees who entered service on or after 01.04.2010 but for All India Service personnel who are in the State Government of Meghalaya, it is applicable from 01.01.2004. The Government employees have to make a contribution of 10% on his/her basic pay plus Dearness Allowances which is deductable from his/her monthly salary bill every month by the DDO and the Government will make an equal matching contribution. The fund is transferred regularly to the Pension Fund Manager.

title: PFMS & DBT | Finance Department Government of Meghalaya
content: PFMS & DBT The integration between TreasuryNET and PFMS has been completed and mapping of various government schemes had been done. PFMS is web-based online transaction system for fund management and e-payment to implementing agencies and beneficiaries through DBT. The objective of PFMS is to establish an efficient fund flow system and expenditure network and provides various stakeholders with a reliable and meaningful management information system and an effective decision support system. A number of State Implementing Agencies have been registered in the online System. Various departments such as Education, Community & Rural Development, Social Welfare, Border Areas, Health, Soil & Water Conservation, etc have incorporated the DBT in transfer of funds under various schemes operated by them. Students have been registered for the appropriate scholarship schemes they are entitled to. Beneficiaries upto the village level are registered for availing various schemes which open up employment avenues, provide necessary day to day services and ensure social security.

title: Treasury NET | Finance Department Government of Meghalaya
content: Treasury NET (opens the full-size chart in a new tab) Treasury NET View full size (opens in a new tab) Download (PNG Size: 104 KB) Online Treasury computerization has been implemented in all District Treasuries and Sub-Treasuries in the State. TreasuryNET is a web-enabled application designed on a n-tier architecture with PHP on the client-end and DB2 is the back-end RDBMS running on Linux O/S. TreasuryNET works on a distributed system architecture in which the central data storage system is housed on a powerful central server and users can access the server from a number of clients located in various treasuries and sub-treasuries throughout the state. TreasuryNET has been designed on a workflow concept where the data (information) flows from the lower level (Counter) to a higher level (Treasury Officer) with different roles to access the data. URL: https://treasurynet.megfinance.gov.in
